items: Set a nonstick skillet (about 10 inches) over medium heat. Add 1/2 tsp of the oil and let it warm for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, garlic powder and coriander. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring every 30 seconds or so, until some beans look a little crisp at the edges.
Add the red pepper and cook for 2 more minutes, stirring, until it is just starting to soften. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and pepper. Spoon the beans and pepper onto your plate.
Put the pan back on medium-low heat with the rest of the oil. Add the spinach and stir for about 30 seconds, until it wilts (shrinks and turns dark green).

Pour in the eggs. Wait 10 seconds, then gently push them around the pan with a spatula. Keep stirring slowly for 1–2 minutes, until there is no runny liquid left. Take the pan off the heat. Season with salt and pepper.
Toast the bread. Put it on the plate with the beans and eggs.

blocks.text: Dressing

**Before you start:** dice the chicken into bite-size pieces. Slice the mushrooms. Rinse the lentils if canned. Dice the red pepper and celery, finely chop the shallot, apricot and almonds, and chop the cilantro.

items: **Cook the bulgur:** put 1 1/2 tbsp dry bulgur in a small bowl, pour over 1/4 cup boiling water, cover and leave 10–12 minutes until soft. Fluff with a fork.
**Mix the spices** in a small bowl. Toss the chicken with half of the mix.

**Cook the chicken and mushrooms:** warm 1 tsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 5–6 minutes, until golden and cooked through (165°F / 74°C inside; no pink when you cut a piece). Add the mushrooms and cook for 3–4 minutes more, until browned. Move everything to a plate.
**Season the lentils:** add the lentils, the rest of the spice mix and 2 tbsp water to the same pan. Stir for 2 minutes, until hot.
**Make the dressing:** whisk the olive oil, vinegar and orange juice.

**Build the bowl:** bulgur on the bottom, then the spiced lentils, then the chicken and mushrooms. Top with the red pepper, celery, shallot, apricot, almonds and cilantro, and drizzle with the dressing.

blocks.text: Built in: raw red bell pepper, plus orange juice in the dressing.
Use 3 oz shredded rotisserie chicken (skip cooking the chicken; iron changes very little); canned lentils; pre-sliced mushrooms; microwave quinoa or rice pouch instead of bulgur.

items: **Vegan:** 5 oz extra-firm tofu, cubed, instead of the chicken (sear the same way).
Gluten-free: quinoa or brown rice instead of bulgur.

blocks.text: Cook the bulgur, chicken, mushrooms and lentils for 2 lunches and store them together. Keep the fresh toppings and dressing separate; reheat, then top.

blocks.text: To serve
Get ready (5 minutes)

items: Turn the oven on to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 3/4-inch cubes (about the size of a large grape).
Dice the onion and the green pepper into small pieces. Mince the garlic (chop it very finely).
Pour the pinto beans into a sieve and rinse them under cold water. Let them drain.

blocks.text: Roast the sweet potato (25 minutes, mostly hands-off)

items: Put the sweet potato cubes on the baking sheet. Add 1/2 tsp oil, the smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper. Toss with your hands until every cube is coated. Spread them out in one layer so they don't touch.
Roast for 20–25 minutes, turning them over with a spatula halfway through. They're done when a fork slides in easily and the edges are browned.

blocks.text: Make the chili (while the potatoes roast)

items: Set a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp oil and let it warm for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and green pepper. Sauté (cook while stirring often) for about 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the beef and a pinch of salt. Break the meat into small crumbles with a wooden spoon. Cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until no pink is left (160°F / 71°C).
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika. Stir for 30 seconds, until the spices smell fragrant.

Add the beans, crushed tomatoes and broth. Stir well. When the chili starts to bubble, turn the heat down to low. Put a lid on the pan, leaving a small gap, and simmer (cook at gentle bubbles) for 15 minutes. Stir every few minutes. If it gets too thick, add a splash of water.
Taste the chili and add more salt and pepper if needed.

blocks.text: Serve

items: Spoon the chili into a bowl. Pile the roasted sweet potato cubes on top of the chili (or serve them in a separate pile next to it if you like them crisp). Sprinkle with cilantro and squeeze the lime wedge over the top.

blocks.text: Edamame quinoa

items: 1/4 cup dry quinoa (makes about 3/4 cup cooked)

blocks.text: Sesame sauce
Sheet pan

items: 4 oz salmon fillet (wild sockeye is leaner)
1/2 red bell pepper, cut into strips

blocks.text: **Before you start:** turn the oven on to 400°F (205°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve. Cut the broccoli into bite-size florets and the pepper into strips.

items: **Cook the quinoa and edamame together:** put the quinoa, frozen edamame, 1/2 cup water and a pinch of salt in a small pan. Bring to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Leave covered. (Or cook them together in a rice cooker on the white rice setting.)
**Make the sauce:** in a small bowl, stir the tamari, rice vinegar, oil, honey, ginger, garlic and sesame seeds.
**Roast the vegetables:** put the broccoli and pepper on the baking sheet. Drizzle with one-third of the sauce and toss with your hands. Spread out and roast for 10 minutes.

**Add the salmon:** take the tray out and push the vegetables to the sides. Put the salmon in the middle, skin side down. Brush it with another third of the sauce. Roast for 10–12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and is no longer see-through in the middle (145°F / 63°C).
**Serve:** spoon the edamame quinoa onto a plate. Add the broccoli, pepper and salmon. Drizzle with the rest of the sauce and sprinkle with green onion.

blocks.text: Burger patty

items: 1/3 cup cooked green, brown or red lentils (rinsed and drained if canned)
1 tsp extra virgin olive oil (for the pan)

blocks.text: To serve

items: 1 romaine leaf, 2 tomato slices, a few thin red onion rings

blocks.text: Sides

items: 1/3 small sweet potato, cut into wedges
1/2 red bell pepper, cut into strips
1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp smoked paprika, salt and black pepper

blocks.text: **Before you start:** turn the oven on to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

items: **Start the wedges:** cut the sweet potato into wedges about 1/2 inch thick. Put them on one side of the baking sheet, toss with 1/2 tsp oil and a pinch of salt and smoked paprika, and spread out. Roast for 10 minutes.

**Add the vegetables:** in a bowl, toss the broccoli and pepper strips with 1 tsp oil, the garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Turn the wedges over and add the vegetables to the other side of the sheet. Roast 12–15 minutes more, until the broccoli edges are crisp and the wedges are soft inside. Squeeze lemon over the broccoli and pepper.

**Make the patty while they roast:** put the lentils in a bowl and mash them with a fork until mostly smooth. Add the beef, flaxseed, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, cumin, a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix with your hands until evenly combined.

Shape into one patty about 3/4 inch thick, slightly wider than the bun (it shrinks as it cooks). Press a small dip in the middle with your thumb so it stays flat. Rest it in the fridge for 10 minutes if you have time — it holds together better.

**Cook the patty:** set a skillet over medium heat with 1 tsp oil. Add the patty and cook for 4–5 minutes without moving it, until browned underneath. Flip carefully with a spatula and cook for 4–5 minutes more, until no pink is left in the middle (160°F / 71°C on a meat thermometer).
**Toast the bun** in the pan or toaster for 1 minute.
**Build the burger:** bun bottom, mustard, romaine, patty, tomato, red onion, bun top. Serve with the sweet potato wedges and roasted broccoli and peppers.
